_comment: THE PRIVACY CONTRACT. This is the ONLY hand-edited definition of what may leave the machine.
scripts/gen_contract.py emits, all committed, all `git diff --exit-code`'d in CI:
Packages/BuilderKit/Sources/BuilderSync/Generated/UploadContract.swift
server/builder/contract.py            (Pydantic, extra='forbid')
mobile/src/generated/contract.ts
web/public/upload-fields.json         (publicly served; what the verification curl fetches)
server/builder/quotes_spec.py         (v4: the quotes document, Pydantic, extra='forbid')
mobile/src/generated/quotes.ts
PRIVACY.md                            (the prose claim, from the same source)
THE STRUCTURAL GUARANTEE IS THE SERIALIZER, NOT THE TEST.
SessionUpload implements encode(to:) by hand as
var c = encoder.container(keyedBy: UploadField.self)
There is NO synthesized Codable and NO hand-written CodingKeys struct anywhere in BuilderSync.
A field absent from the generated UploadField enum is UNREPRESENTABLE ON THE WIRE. Adding a
stored property to any model therefore cannot change the payload. Deleting a line from this
file deletes a field from the product.
NOT PRESENT, AND NOT ADDABLE WITHOUT EDITING THIS FILE:
prompt text, assistant text, thinking blocks, tool inputs, tool outputs, file contents,
diffs, structuredPatch, file paths, file NAMES, directory names, commit MESSAGES,
commit SHAs, BRANCH NAMES, cwd, git origin URL, repo names for anonymous repos,
MCP server names, terminal commands or output, environment variables, URLs fetched,
hostname, IP address.
THE ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION (v2): `analysis`. It is model-written prose about the session,
produced on the user's own machine by their own Claude Code from a digest of the transcript,
and its shape is fixed by spec/analysis.v1.json (every string bounded, extra keys rejected).
It may name files and features in prose, and `decision_patterns[].prompt_excerpt` carries
SHORT VERBATIM PROMPT QUOTES, capped at 160 characters each. It is OPT-IN, nullable, omitted
from the wire when off, private to the account under RLS, and leaves the account only when
the session is explicitly shared. Everything else on the list above still holds: no field
outside `analysis` carries prose, and `analysis` itself carries no paths, diffs, tool I/O,
commit messages, branch names, URLs, hostnames or raw prompts.
THE SECOND FIELD ADDED SINCE v2 (v3): `feedback`. What ONE sitting cost you, for the card you
read once and close: a stretch that went nowhere, a run of failures, a file rewritten over and
over. It is NOT a second `analysis` and needed no exception, because it carries no prose at all
— an id from a fixed list of three, and two integers. The SENTENCE is written on the phone from
that id, so nothing about the wording travels either.
What it deliberately does NOT carry, and both were in the local version of these notes:
* the FAILING COMMAND. `analysis/feedback.py` says "4 failures in a row on `bun test`" on your
own machine. Terminal commands are on the never-list above and stay there; the wire says how
many and for how long.
* the FILE NAME. The local note names the file that was rewritten five times. `analysis` may
name files in prose because it is opt-in and bounded; this field is neither, so it says
"a file" and the name stays on the machine.
Two design contradictions resolved here, deliberately:
1. Branch names are DELETED ENTIRELY. One design's never-list banned them while another
uploaded them for public repos. Branch was read by zero cards and zero queries, so
deleting it makes both documents true at zero product cost. 'feat/acquisition-flow'
leaks roadmap more reliably than a repo name does.
2. NO PROMPT OR FILE NAME LEAVES IN ANY MODE. Three designs built a server titling
endpoint carrying first_prompt/last_prompt/commit_messages/file_basenames. It is
deleted, not restricted — every harness already writes a title to disk. This is also
what makes the falsification command on /privacy safe to publish.
v4 (2026-09-13, docs/overnight-integration.md section 2). Everything below is ids, numbers, enums and clocks unless it says OPT-IN.
* `tool_calls` names its allowlist as data (`values`), and the server rejects a key outside it: the doc always promised that
unknown and MCP names bucket to mcp_other and other, and now the door keeps the promise.
* `live`: what a RUNNING session is doing, shaped by spec/live.v1.json. Enums, integers, clocks and 16 hex salted file ids. No
path, file name, command, prompt or sentence. Deleted when the session is final.
* `live_names`: THE THIRD OPT-IN EXCEPTION. The basename of each file in the live map, off by default, sent only with
`capture sync --live --live-names`, stored only while the account has File names on, shown only on the session screen.
* `burn` and `title_ids`: where a sitting's tokens went, and its engineer voice title, as numbers and ids (`objects` below).
The sentences are written on the phone; no word, path or command travels.
* `call_tokens`: what every call to the model sent and got back, as at most 240 points of five token counts, the calls that
came back to an expired cache and the list price of each bucket (`objects` below). Numbers and two enums: no word, no model name.
* `quotes`: THE SECOND OPT-IN EXCEPTION, a document of its own with its own route, modelled on `analysis`: up to three prompts
verbatim, for the Wrapped cards that quote you. Off unless the phone's setting AND the machine's --quotes flag both say yes.
_excluded_note: visibility 'excluded' is not a mode: an excluded repo produces ZERO uploads, and if ANY event in a session resolves to an excluded repo the ENTIRE session is dropped — never partially uploaded, never uploaded under the primary repo's visibility.

fields.name: client_session_id
fields.doc: stable opaque session id; also the Idempotency-Key

fields.name: machine_id
fields.doc: sha256 of this Mac's platform UUID

fields.name: content_hash
fields.doc: hash of this payload; lets sync skip unchanged sessions

fields.name: client_version
fields.doc: agent version

fields.name: sessionizer_version
fields.doc: so a retuned boundary is a recompute, not a migration

fields.name: active_calc_version
fields.doc: so a retuned active-time formula is a recompute

fields.name: agent_observed_at
fields.doc: when the agent produced this payload: the finalize instant for final, the snapshot instant for live

fields.name: client_clock_offset_ms
fields.doc: measured against the server Date header

fields.name: active_seconds
fields.doc: union of turn spans and capped gaps; the honest headline

fields.name: state
fields.doc: live = an open/idle session snapshot, replaced in place when it finalizes; final = complete

fields.name: end_reason
fields.doc: why the session ended (docs/session-boundaries.md). still_running IS the live upload; cleared (a typed /clear) and switched_repo (a new session opened in another repo) are v3 ends that, like idle_gap, mean the work stopped

fields.name: attended_seconds
fields.doc: active time with a human evidently present (docs/session-boundaries.md)

fields.name: autonomous_seconds
fields.doc: active time after the human went quiet for > tauAutonomousSec

fields.name: presence_count
fields.doc: typed prompts + interrupts + human file edits

fields.name: unattended
fields.doc: zero presence signals. Hours only: no record, no streak, no notification

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: counts toward hours, graph, streaks

fields.name: notable
fields.doc: eligible for a card or a record

fields.name: strip_columns
fields.doc: 1024 bytes: 2-bit class, 2-bit density. No text, no paths, by construction

fields.name: strip_marks
fields.doc: [{ms, k}] where k is prompt, commit or compact

fields.name: prompt_count_basis
fields.doc: so Cursor's looser rule never sums with Claude Code's

fields.name: tool_calls
fields.doc: allowlisted tool names only; unknown and MCP names bucket to mcp_other / other

fields.name: lines_added_agent
fields.doc: live-path only; rewound edits never landed

fields.name: human_edit_events
fields.doc: count of edited_text_file / humanChanges signals. Existence only: these carry no line counts

fields.name: agent_line_bucket
fields.doc: a 5-way LOWER BOUND, never a percentage

fields.name: tokens_reported
fields.doc: false for EVERY Cursor session, forever: Cursor never writes token counts locally

fields.name: tokens
fields.doc: five separate buckets. Null, never zero, when unreported

fields.name: abandoned_branch_tokens
fields.doc: tokens spent on rewound DAG branches. You paid for them

fields.name: token_dedupe
fields.doc: server rejects none + tokens_reported: that is the 1.88x arriving unlabeled

fields.name: token_scope
fields.doc: 'flat' is NOT a legal value: it would let the ~3x subagent glob overcount in wearing a legitimate label

fields.name: models
fields.doc: [{model_id, output_token_share}], labels only. The [1m] suffix is preserved verbatim

fields.name: model_state
fields.doc: Cursor is ~84% unknown: modelName is 'default' on 115 of 137 composers

fields.name: repo_hash
fields.doc: HMAC of the normalized origin URL. Full 64 hex, never truncated

fields.name: repo_name
fields.doc: PUBLIC REPOS ONLY. Absent from the anonymous key set entirely

fields.name: title
fields.doc: PUBLIC REPOS ONLY. The title the HARNESS already wrote to your disk. Never model-generated by us

fields.name: card_png_url
fields.doc: populated ONLY when you tap Share. The image you chose to publish; contains no field not listed above

fields.name: analysis
fields.doc: model-written reading of the session, produced on the user's machine by their own Claude Code from a digest of the transcript (spec/analysis.v1.json). Present only when analysis upload is enabled. Private to the account under RLS; leaves it only when the session is shared. This is the ONE field that carries prose derived from prompts and code, and it is opt-in for exactly that reason.

fields.name: feedback
fields.doc: what this one sitting cost that you would not have chosen: [{id, seconds, count}] where id is one of three fixed notes. Numbers only: no command, no file name, no prose. Computed on the machine (analysis/feedback.py); the sentence is rendered on the phone. Null, never [], when the sitting had nothing worth saying

fields.name: live
fields.doc: what a RUNNING session is doing now (spec/live.v1.json): enums, integers, clocks and 16 hex salted file ids. No path, file name, command, prompt or sentence. Only on state=live payloads; deleted when the session is final.

fields.name: live_names
fields.doc: OPT-IN, OFF BY DEFAULT: the basename of each file in live.map, keyed by its id. Sent only with `capture sync --live --live-names` and stored only while the account has File names on. Owner only; shown on the session screen, never on the Lock Screen, the widget, a push or a share.

fields.name: burn
fields.doc: where this sitting's tokens went and whether anything came of it (analysis/burn.py over the session window): counts, shares, enums and at most three costly stretches. No prompt, path, command, file name or tool name. Computed on the machine or by the hook channel; the phone writes every sentence. Null when the producer does not compute it; a refusal is burn.reason, never a zero.

fields.name: title_ids
fields.doc: an engineer voice title as ids (analysis/vocab.py session_title): a verb and an object from fixed tables and the numbers the title says. The phone renders the words from them; no file or directory name travels. A refusal is title_ids.reason with no verb or object, and it replaces a title stored before; null means only that the producer does not compute titles.

fields.name: call_tokens
fields.doc: what every call to the model sent and got back in this sitting (analysis/calls.py over the session window, each message counted once): at most 240 points of five token counts, the calls that came back to an expired cache, and the list price of each kind of token. Numbers and two enums: no prompt, path, command, file name, tool name or model name. Computed on the machine or by the hook channel; the phone draws the chart and writes every sentence. Null when the producer does not compute it; a refusal is call_tokens.reason, never a zero.

_objects_note: The shapes of the three structured session fields added in v4, `burn`, `title_ids` and `call_tokens`, in the notation of spec/*.json
(scripts/gen_analysis.py's emitters read it). Numbers, bools and enums only: server/tests/test_contract.py fails on any
string field here. Every enum copies a Python table and is pinned to it both ways by that test: burn_cause to
analysis/burn.py _CAUSE_SENTENCES and the causes Segment detects, burn_repeat to burn._REPEAT_SENTENCES, title_verb,
title_object and title_refusal to analysis/vocab.py VERBS, OBJECTS and TITLE_REFUSALS; burn_refusal equals spec/report.v1.json's burn_refusal, one list of codes
for one module's refusals; call_tokens_refusal to analysis/calls.py REFUSALS and call_price_refusal to calls.PRICE_REFUSALS (pricing's own code).
A double is a 0 to 1 share and a number is a count of dollars at API list prices. The sentences are written on the phone from these
(burn.explain is the reference; spec/fixtures/burn/session.json pins the port), so nothing here carries a word.

SessionBurnCause.name: n
SessionBurnCause.doc: the count behind the cause: helpers dispatched, failing results, copies of one call, rewrites of one file, cache read tokens for context_replay, compactions, reads

SessionBurnCause.name: tokens
SessionBurnCause.doc: the tokens this cause can claim out of the segment (burn.Segment.attribution). Claims overlap, so they never sum. Null when the segment carries no token counts

SessionBurnCause.name: repeat
SessionBurnCause.doc: repeated_call only: what repeated (burn._repeat_kind), so the phrase says a command only when one was. Null for every other cause

SessionBurnSpike.name: multiple
SessionBurnSpike.doc: its tokens over the session's median segment, 1 dp

SessionBurnSpike.name: barren
SessionBurnSpike.doc: it spent tokens and provably changed nothing (burn.Segment.barren)

SessionBurnSpike.name: seconds
SessionBurnSpike.doc: from its prompt to its last event

SessionBurnSpike.name: causes
SessionBurnSpike.doc: why it cost what it did: the causes claiming the most tokens, most first, ties in burn's order, so causes[0] is burn's dominant cause whenever one claims a token. [] when no cause was detected

SessionBurnSpike.name: files_changed
SessionBurnSpike.doc: files it changed, less the calls an error answered (burn.Segment.files_touched); the stretch's verdict reads it

SessionBurnSpike.name: commits
SessionBurnSpike.doc: commit calls in it no error answered (burn.Segment.commits)

SessionBurnSpike.name: unreadable
SessionBurnSpike.doc: no visible work, but it ran something that could have changed a file the transcript does not show (burn.Segment.unreadable), so its verdict says it cannot be read rather than that nothing was written

SessionBurn.name: tokens
SessionBurn.doc: tokens inside this session's segments over its window, every assistant message counted once (burn.segments over burn.turns_for_window, deduplicated on message id). Null when refused, never 0 standing in for not counted

SessionBurn.name: cache_read_share
SessionBurn.doc: share of tokens served from cache, the conversation re-reading itself. Not rounded: the phone rounds once, as burn._unrounded does. Null exactly when tokens is

SessionBurn.name: barren_share
SessionBurn.doc: share of tokens spent in segments that provably changed nothing (burn.Segment.barren). Not rounded. Null exactly when tokens is

SessionBurn.name: unreadable_share
SessionBurn.doc: share of tokens spent in segments with no visible work whose scripts, builds or helper agents could have changed files the transcript does not show (burn.Segment.unreadable): neither barren nor productive. Not rounded. Null exactly when tokens is

SessionBurn.name: segments
SessionBurn.doc: segments the window was cut into, one human prompt to the next (burn.segments); 0 only with reason not_segmented

SessionBurn.name: lines_added
SessionBurn.doc: lines added across the segments (burn.Segment.lines_added: edit tools plus credited shell writes), the count the summary's first sentence reads. Null when the window held no events

SessionBurn.name: lines_removed
SessionBurn.doc: lines removed across the segments (burn.Segment.lines_removed). Null when the window held no events

SessionBurn.name: files_changed
SessionBurn.doc: distinct files a call changed and no error answered, over the window (burn's rule, the one live's files_changed reads). Not files_touched, which counts every file named. Null when the window held no events

SessionBurn.name: commits
SessionBurn.doc: commit calls no error answered, summed over the segments (burn.Segment.commits). Not commit_count, which is git log. Null when the window held no events

SessionBurn.name: reason
SessionBurn.doc: why tokens and the shares are null: no_token_counts (the transcript records no usage), not_segmented (no events to cut into segments), nothing_inside_segments (usage recorded, but no token fell inside a segment). below_session_floor is the corpus block's and never appears on a session. Null when answered

SessionBurn.name: spikes
SessionBurn.doc: the costliest segments that cost at least burn.SPIKE_MULTIPLE times the median segment, most expensive first. Null when no spike can be named: reason is set, or segments is under spikes_needed, where a median would be an accident. [] only when enough segments were measured and none cleared the bar

SessionBurn.name: spikes_needed
SessionBurn.doc: burn.MIN_SEGMENTS_FOR_SPIKES, the segments a median needs before any segment is called a spike, so the phone can say why spikes is null

SessionTitleIds.name: verb
SessionTitleIds.doc: the first title rule the session satisfied (vocab.VERBS, in the order they are tried). Null exactly when reason is set

SessionTitleIds.name: object
SessionTitleIds.doc: what the title is about: a file role, or test_suite, commit, failure, codebase (vocab.OBJECTS). Null exactly when reason is set

SessionTitleIds.name: n
SessionTitleIds.doc: the number the title says (vocab session_title count): files of that role, migrations, commits, recoveries, or failures in a row. Null only for looked_around

SessionTitleIds.name: modules
SessionTitleIds.doc: distinct directories the project files were written in, the refactor title's second number (vocab session_title modules). Null when no project file was written

SessionTitleIds.name: reason
SessionTitleIds.doc: why no title rule fired (vocab.TITLE_REFUSALS): no_tool_calls, writes_name_no_file (a harness that does not say which file a patch touched), harness_files_only (only Claude Code's own scratch or notes were written), below_checkpoint_density (too few visible writes, tests or commits for a title to describe the work rather than what the transcript hides). Null when a title answered

SessionCallPoint.name: at
SessionCallPoint.doc: seconds from the session's start to the first call in this point

SessionCallPoint.name: cache_read
SessionCallPoint.doc: tokens re-read from the cache (cache_read_input_tokens), summed over the point's calls: the conversation so far, sent again

SessionCallPoint.name: cache_write
SessionCallPoint.doc: tokens written to the cache (cache_creation_input_tokens, both lifetimes): what was new in the conversation, or all of it again after the cache expired

SessionCallPoint.name: input
SessionCallPoint.doc: fresh input tokens, neither read from nor written to the cache

SessionCallRewrite.name: call
SessionCallRewrite.doc: the call's number in this session, counting from 1; the first per_point calls are the first point, the next per_point the second

SessionCallRewrite.name: away_seconds
SessionCallRewrite.doc: seconds since the call before it in the same transcript, which can sit in an earlier session: longer than lifetime_seconds

SessionCallRewrite.name: written
SessionCallRewrite.doc: the tokens it wrote to the cache again, more than half of everything it sent (calls.REWRITE_MIN_SHARE)

SessionCallTokens.name: reason
SessionCallTokens.doc: why there is no chart: no_token_counts (the transcript records no usage, or the harness is one burn does not read yet), too_few_calls (fewer than calls_needed). Null when answered; then every field below that can be is set

SessionCallTokens.name: calls
SessionCallTokens.doc: calls to the model in the session window, each assistant message once and `<synthetic>` placeholders left out (calls.calls_of). Null only with reason no_token_counts, where nothing was counted

SessionCallTokens.name: calls_needed
SessionCallTokens.doc: calls.MIN_CALLS, the calls a chart needs, so the phone can say why a short session has none

SessionCallTokens.name: per_point
SessionCallTokens.doc: consecutive calls summed into each point: 1 up to 240 calls, then ceil(calls / 240), the last point holding the rest. Null when refused

SessionCallTokens.name: points
SessionCallTokens.doc: the calls in time order, per_point to a point. Their tokens sum to the tokens burn counts for the same window. Null when refused

SessionCallTokens.name: lifetime_seconds
SessionCallTokens.doc: how long the cache kept what these calls wrote: 3600 when any call wrote with the one hour lifetime, 300 when they wrote only with five minutes, null when nothing was written to a cache (then no call is a rewrite) or when refused

SessionCallTokens.name: rewrites
SessionCallTokens.doc: calls that came back to an expired cache and wrote most of the conversation into it again, the 12 that wrote the most, in call order. [] when none did; null when refused

SessionCallTokens.name: rewrite_calls
SessionCallTokens.doc: every such call, however many rewrites keeps. Null when refused

SessionCallTokens.name: usd_cache_read
SessionCallTokens.doc: the re-reads at API list prices, dollars, each call priced on its own model (analysis/pricing.py cost_usd). Never a bill. Null when refused or when price_reason is set

SessionCallTokens.name: usd_cache_write
SessionCallTokens.doc: the cache writes at API list prices, dollars, the five minute and the one hour writes each at its own rate. Null when refused or when price_reason is set

SessionCallTokens.name: usd_input
SessionCallTokens.doc: the fresh input at API list prices, dollars. Null when refused or when price_reason is set

SessionCallTokens.name: usd_output
SessionCallTokens.doc: what the model wrote back at API list prices, dollars. Null when refused or when price_reason is set

SessionCallTokens.name: price_reason
SessionCallTokens.doc: why the four dollar fields are null on an answered chart: model_not_in_price_table (a call that carries tokens names a model analysis/pricing.py has no price for, so it is not priced at a guess). Null otherwise

doc: THE SECOND OPT-IN EXCEPTION (v4). Up to three prompts, verbatim, for the Wrapped cards that quote you. Off until BOTH Settings on the phone
and --quotes on the machine say yes. Masked, identifier filtered twice. Owner only; never in a post, feed, share, push or activity. Off deletes.

QuoteWire.name: text
QuoteWire.doc: wrapped._quote: whitespace collapsed, cut at the last space inside 160

QuoteWire.name: client_session_id
QuoteWire.doc: the session it was sent in, already on the server

QuoteWire.name: seconds_in
QuoteWire.doc: from that session's start to this prompt (the crash out sentence)
